name: Beethoven
description:
**Ludwig van Beethoven (December 16, 1770 – March 26, 1827): Inheriting the Classical Tradition, Ushering in the Romantic Era**

Ludwig van Beethoven (German: Ludwig van Beethoven), a German composer and pianist, inherited the rigor and tradition of the Classical period while pioneering the emotion and spirit of freedom in the Romantic era, making him an extremely important figure in music history[1]. Despite gradually losing his hearing throughout his life, Beethoven persevered in his creative work, transcending the pain of reality to bring his art to its zenith, writing works that are immortalized in music history, such as nine symphonies, 36 piano sonatas (32 of which are numbered, with one unfinished), 10 violin sonatas, 16 string quartets, one opera, and two masses. His innovations in musical form, harmony, and texture had profound influence, with his 32 piano sonatas, and the Third, Fifth, Sixth, and Ninth Symphonies, along with the "Missa Solemnis," being particularly renowned[2][3]. In 1827, Beethoven died of illness. As one of the pioneers who advanced the development of Western music, he has long been revered in Chinese-speaking cultures as the "Saint of Music."

---

### Growth and Early Life

Beethoven was born in Bonn, the capital of the Electorate of Cologne in the Holy Roman Empire. His father, Johann van Beethoven, was a tenor singer in the choir who was skilled at cultivating musical talent in children. His great-grandfather, Michael van Beethoven, came from the Flemish region of present-day Belgium, while his mother, Maria Magdalena Keverich, came from a family of court chefs. The couple settled in Bonn in their early years and gave birth to Beethoven there. The "van" in Beethoven's name is Flemish, not the German "von," and therefore does not denote noble title[5][9]. Beethoven's innate musical talent led his father to hope he could become a child prodigy like Mozart.

Growing up in a musical environment, Beethoven received his musical education from his father and showed astonishing musical talent from an early age. However, his father's music education was filled with violence and excessive strictness, and Beethoven's childhood was spent under the dual pressure of music and harsh discipline. Due to the family's poor financial situation, Beethoven had to shoulder part of the family's responsibilities at an early age. Beethoven displayed musical talent in his youth, beginning piano training at age six and giving his first public performance at eight. By eleven, he was already serving as an organist in the local theater orchestra and had published three sonatas. Despite achieving some musical success, his father's harsh training and the tense atmosphere within the family meant Beethoven's childhood was not a happy one.

Although Johann Beethoven's education was strict and violent, he realized he could no longer provide his son with higher musical instruction, so he arranged for Christian Gottlob Neefe, then the court music director in Bonn, to be Beethoven's composition and piano teacher. Under his teacher's careful guidance, Beethoven gradually displayed astonishing musical talent. In 1782, Beethoven took his teacher's place as the court orchestra's harpsichordist, not only beginning with light pieces but also actively studying the works of musical predecessors such as Mozart and Bach.

---

### Initial Musical Education and Departure for Vienna

In 1792, after receiving support from Archbishop-Elector Maximilian Franz, Beethoven conceived the idea of going to Vienna to study. It is said that during a brief visit to Vienna afterward, Beethoven was able to meet Mozart, though this experience is not supported by clear historical records. Legend has it that when Mozart heard Beethoven's improvisation, he commented that "he will surely make a name for himself in the future." [Details about the brief 1787 Vienna visit need to be supplemented] However, due to his mother's serious illness and death, Beethoven ended his Vienna apprenticeship and returned home early. It wasn't until 1792, when he was not yet twenty, that with Haydn's encouragement and support, Beethoven decided to return to Vienna, officially beginning what would be a 35-year musical journey.

After arriving in Vienna, although Beethoven studied composition with Haydn, their teacher-student relationship was not particularly smooth due to differences in musical philosophy and personality. The elderly Haydn found it difficult to devote enough time to thoroughly instruct Beethoven. Beethoven subsequently turned to study counterpoint with the renowned musician Johann Georg Albrechtsberger, while Salieri and others helped Beethoven further improve his vocal and compositional skills.

---

### Rising to Prominence and Career as a Vienna Soloist

In his first few years in Vienna, through his own tireless efforts, Beethoven gradually became a rising star in the music world. Early patrons such as Prince Lichnowsky and Count Razumovsky provided Beethoven with extensive support. In 1795, Beethoven made his debut as a pianist in Vienna with his own "Piano Concerto No. 2 in B-flat Major," a performance that achieved tremendous success and won him widespread recognition among musicians. This marked his official entrance as both a performer and composer in Vienna's music scene.

In 1799, Beethoven composed the "Piano Sonata No. 8 in C minor," also known as the "Pathétique Sonata"[36]. This work was widely beloved and not only demonstrated Beethoven's interest in dramatic musical expression but also established his important position in the contemporary music world. Beethoven then embarked on a series of piano sonatas and chamber music compositions, with works such as the "Spring Sonata" and "Symphony No. 1" also achieving great success and displaying a distinctive Classical style. The compositions from this period laid the foundation for his subsequent "Heroic Period" works.

---

### The "Eroica Symphony" and Beethoven at His Peak

Entering the early 1800s, Beethoven's compositional skills reached maturity, entering the creative peak of his life. As a musical star in Vienna, Beethoven was not only highly revered in social circles but his works were also market favorites. At the same time, Beethoven's ear disease began to worsen, affecting his sense of hearing. Nevertheless, Beethoven's passion for music and his indomitable will drove him ever forward[35].

In 1803, Beethoven completed an epoch-making symphonic work—the Third Symphony, widely known as the "Eroica Symphony" (Opus 55). This work was originally dedicated to Napoleon, but when news of Napoleon's coronation as emperor reached Vienna, Beethoven felt disappointed and even angry, believing that Napoleon had betrayed the republican and liberal ideals he pursued. He decided to withdraw the dedication to Napoleon, tore off the dedication page, and renamed the symphony the "Eroica Symphony"[48][49]. Unlike previous symphonies, the "Eroica Symphony" was grand in scale, profound and intense in emotion, and more epic in spirit. It marked that Beethoven's creative level had reached an unprecedented height.

The "Eroica Symphony" opened up a new creative world. In Beethoven's symphonic history, the Eroica Symphony has a pioneering spirit—it was no longer written for a specific class or patron, but rather a broad emotional presentation transcending any particular group, focusing on ideals beyond the individual—freedom, political liberation, and human fellowship. This work also represented that Beethoven's creative style had undergone a transformation, moving from Classical to Romantic, and clearly expressing his strong personal desires regarding society, politics, and life.

Thereafter, he continued to create works such as "Symphony No. 4 in G Major" and the "Appassionata Sonata," maintaining a highly productive state. Especially the Fifth and Sixth Symphonies, which premiered together in 1808, marked two typical examples of Beethoven's different musical styles: the struggle and tension of the C minor Fifth Symphony, the "Fate Symphony," and the leisurely naturalness of the F major Sixth Symphony, the "Pastoral Symphony," forming a striking contrast. The opening four notes of the Fifth Symphony were hailed as "fate knocking at the door," becoming a universally known classic melody[39].

---

### Late Works and Creative Zenith: "Missa Solemnis" and "Symphony No. 9"

As his ear disease further deteriorated, by 1814, Beethoven had become almost completely deaf, yet his creative work increasingly reached its artistic zenith. Late-period Beethoven created immortal works such as the Seventh Symphony in G Major and the Ninth Symphony in A Major. His reflections on the world, life, and fate were continuously infused into his musical works, ultimately forming masterpieces embodying his ultimate musical spirit—"Symphony No. 9"[35].

The creation of Beethoven's "Symphony No. 9" was no accident. As early as 1793, he had conceived the idea of setting Schiller's poem "Ode to Joy" to music. The emotionally uplifting choral section is like a spiritual resonance of humanity's pursuit of beauty and lasting peace. The "Ode to Joy" theme in the fourth movement continuously deepens, symbolizing Beethoven's concern for human destiny and dignity behind his musical thinking. When "Symphony No. 9" premiered in Vienna in 1824, although Beethoven at the conductor's podium could hear nothing at all, the audience's applause and cheers continued for a long time[82].

Another important religious work from Beethoven's late period, the "Missa Solemnis," was composed for the installation ceremony of his student and patron, Archduke Rudolf. Four years of arduous creation integrated Beethoven's profound late-period reflections on life, displaying his major contemplations on religion[35].

---

### Final Years and Death

With the complete loss of his hearing, Beethoven in his final years had almost lost the means of normal communication with the outside world and had to communicate through conversation books. Nevertheless, he continued to create some great works. On March 26, 1827, Beethoven passed away after long suffering from cirrhosis of the liver and various other diseases.

Beethoven's death marked the end of Classical music and the birth of Romanticism. At his funeral, tens of thousands of Viennese citizens turned out to see off this musical giant, with musicians such as Schubert personally serving as pallbearers to pay their respects[83].

### Beethoven's Musical Achievements and Influence

Beethoven's works embody his innovative spirit and relentless pursuit of musical art forms. His 32 piano sonatas, nine symphonies, late string quartets, and one opera "Fidelio" had profound influence on music history both in form and content. They are hailed by later generations as the beginning of Romantic music and had an enormous inspiring effect on 19th-century composers such as Brahms and Wagner.

Beethoven's music broke through the Classical period's sense of propriety and rationality to a certain degree, injecting personal emotions and experiences into music. Although most of his life was accompanied by pain and loneliness, Beethoven always maintained his love for the art of music. Even when living conditions were extremely harsh, Beethoven never abandoned his artistic pursuits, using music to dialogue with himself.

It can be said that it was precisely Beethoven's spirit of struggling against fate and the emotional depth he imbued in his music that opened a new chapter in music history. For this reason, he has earned the deep reverence of countless later generations and is honored as the "Saint of Music."

name: Luffy
description:
Monkey D. Luffy is the central character of "ONE PIECE," one of the "D" clan, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates and leader of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet, and one of the three main fighters. He's a sunny youth with short black hair and a scar below his left eye—a mark he gave himself with a knife as a child to prove his bravery to "Red-Haired" Shanks. His iconic "straw hat" was entrusted to him by his childhood idol "Red-Haired" Shanks for safekeeping (the hat's original owner was Gol D. Roger), which is why he's often called "Straw Hat Boy." Thanks to the Spartan training regimen imposed by his grandfather (Vice Admiral Monkey D. Garp of the Navy Headquarters), he developed incredibly tenacious vitality. In his youth, he accidentally ate a Devil Fruit from the Paramecia class called the "Gum-Gum Fruit," turning him into a rubber man whose entire body—from skin to blood vessels—can stretch and contract. As the story progresses, it's revealed that this fruit has another name: the Zoan-type Mythical "Human-Human Fruit, Nika Model."

His personality shares many similarities with "Pirate King" Gol D. Roger, such as loving parties and freedom. The nature of his Conqueror's Haki is the same as Roger's, and media reporters have identified him as Roger's successor. He has a cheerful disposition, absolutely loves eating meat—especially meat on the bone. His appetite is enormous, calculated at five meals a day, and he can do many things simultaneously. He deeply values his crewmates but lacks common sense and has no concept of navigation. Sometimes he makes things worse, always requiring his crew to clean up after him.

Luffy only sleeps five hours a day. He's the type who sleeps when he's tired and gets up when he feels like it. He tends to doze off when listening to others talk, sometimes even falling asleep mid-conversation. Because he constantly introduces himself by name, he's terrible at covert operations, but he never reflects on this. He dreams of becoming the Pirate King, believing that "the freest person on this sea is the Pirate King." To uphold the dignity of pirates, young Luffy didn't hesitate to risk his life challenging mountain bandits. Unlike other pirates, he doesn't kill indiscriminately in pursuit of wealth. He has a strong sense of justice but hates being treated as a hero (because Luffy thinks heroes have to share their food with others), instead enjoying the adventure of being a pirate. His catchphrase is "I'm gonna be the Pirate King!" (Japanese: 海賊王に、おれはなる!). Oda has also mentioned that if the Straw Hat Pirates were a large family, Luffy would be the fourth son. In Robin's mind, the flower that represents Luffy is the cosmos.

name: Nobita Nobi
description:
Nobita Nobi is the protagonist of Fujiko F. Fujio's manga and anime series "Doraemon."

According to some manga sources, Nobita was born on August 7th and lives at Suzukihara Road, Tsukimidai, Nerima Ward, Tokyo, Japan. Although times have changed, he consistently appears as an elementary school student living in Tokyo, perpetually ten years old (in the manga, he's always a fourth-grader; in the early Ōyama version of the anime, he was in fourth grade and often suffered from "Gian, dogs, and ditches," while in the later Ōyama version and the Mizuta version, he became a fifth-grader). He's an only child living with his parents and Doraemon.

The meaning behind his parents' choice of name:

Manga
- "We hope he'll grow up healthy and keep progressing no matter what."
Anime
- Ōyama version: They hoped he would grow up safely and become a strong and mighty person.
- The name "Kang Fu" used in the CCTV broadcast version in mainland China carries the meaning of "healthy growth."

Adult Nobita occasionally appears in the series, mostly when elementary school student Nobita uses the time machine to visit the future or observes through devices like the time TV. Adult Nobita no longer wears glasses because his nearsightedness has been cured; he originally became nearsighted in second grade. Additionally, both Nobita and his mother have big, watery eyes, with young Nobita being proof of this. It's just that adult Nobita usually wears glasses so you can't tell, and when he takes them off, his eyes are deliberately drawn in a squinting shape. However, in theatrical versions and some TV episodes, there are scenes showing Nobita's big eyes. In "When Mom Became an Elementary Student," when Tamako Nobi turned into a child, she also didn't wear glasses and looked somewhat like Shizuka.

Strengths
- Fundamentally kind-hearted and willing to help others, showing compassion for animals, plants, and even toys (with some exceptions). He's willing to give up his own gifts to make others happy and sometimes asks Doraemon to use gadgets to help others.
- Loves nature and cares for animals and plants. Although he's often bitten by dogs, he still loves them. Despite his mother not allowing him to keep pets, he frequently brings injured animals home to care for them.
- Has excellent judgment about manga; any work he finds interesting eventually becomes famous, despite his own poor drawing skills.
- In critical moments during the feature-length stories, he often shows brave and outstanding performance, especially in later works.
- Sometimes tries to work hard and face difficulties on his own, though he can usually only maintain this for a short time. There are things he's continuously improved at over time.
- Stubbornly adheres to what's right, especially evident in the feature-length stories.
- Frequently reflects on himself. Although he quickly reverts to his old ways after reflecting, he does self-reflect after every mistake. Fujiko F. Fujio mentioned in a program that he finds this quality of Nobita's remarkable.
- More environmentally conscious than others (except regarding food), sometimes reusing damaged items.
- Sometimes very clever at using Doraemon's gadgets in unexpected ways, though mostly through small tricks. Even when Doraemon isn't fully familiar with all the functions of his miraculous gadgets, Nobita can enhance their utility with various unpredictable creative ideas and clever tricks.
- Very popular with girls; in some anime episodes and feature-length stories, you can see Nobita having many interactions with numerous girls.
- Can easily lift Doraemon, who weighs 129.3 kilograms, proving that Nobita actually has considerable strength and is stronger than Shizuka and Suneo.
- According to the Doraemon guidebook, Nobita actually possesses extremely strong athletic ability: he instantly learned roller skating (Volume 3, "Nobita's Kingdom"), can easily play kendama with his toes and toss paper balls into trash cans, can jump 30 centimeters from a standing position, and in Volume 11's "What-If Phone Booth," he could run at high speed pulling a kite. In "Good Child Headband," he kicked away Gian, who's heavier than himself, using his own strength, and after a huge steel beam fell directly on his head from a height, he could get up within seconds. This shows Nobita has considerable talent in body balance, strength, jumping ability, resistance to impact, and speed. Despite these abilities that defy common sense, he's unwilling to play baseball or fight.
- According to the Doraemon guidebook, Nobita frequently uses the library to read books, and in "Nobita Juice," he created bacteria that even Doraemon had difficulty producing successfully.
- Friendly and open-minded toward all beings, whether human or other species, including aliens—he's willing to actively communicate with them all.
- According to the Doraemon guidebook, Nobita has exceptional business talent and adheres to his own business principles. For example, in "Using Mirrors for Advertising," he saved a confectionery shop from bankruptcy. In "Selling the Night," he made quite a bit of money using night bulbs. Although Nobita's academic performance is poor, he possesses skills that are absolutely not inferior to others. It's just that the adults around him only evaluate him by the same old standards, so his talents in cat's cradle, falling asleep within 0.93 seconds, fancy eating, and shooting haven't been properly valued.
- Nobita can't even answer basic questions on his homework assignments. However, in Volume 11, an anomaly appeared. In Volume 11's "Speed-Up Screw," after using the speed-up screw, Nobita quickly finished his homework. This wasn't entirely due to the gadget's ability—the speed-up screw only made his movements efficient; his thinking couldn't keep up. This proves Nobita has the ability to do it himself.

Weaknesses
- Poor academic performance, lacks common sense, getting zero on tests is routine
    - He's only gotten 100 points on arithmetic tests three times; he's quite satisfied just getting ten points, and getting 30 points makes his mom quite happy, though when she's in a bad mood, she finds 50 points quite ordinary. This contrasts sharply with Shizuka, who gets scolded by her mom for getting 85 points. On average, one out of every five tests he takes is a zero (some versions say three zeros out of every ten tests). He once celebrated getting only one zero out of ten tests, considering it progress.
    - Can't even write his own name correctly, often writing 野比のび太 (the character "太" is a third-grade kanji in Japan) as 野比のび犬 (the character "犬" is a first-grade kanji in Japan) (translated as "Dog Hero" in Taiwan and mainland China).
    - Has low expectations for himself. Nobita once hoped that Tamoku, a classmate who performed worse than him, would remain poor alongside him, but ultimately Tamoku didn't participate with Nobita because he wanted to pursue improvement. ("Someone Worse Than Nobita Arrived")
    - Simple-minded, easily deceived by Gian and Suneo's lies
    - Playful, uses gadgets to play pranks on others
- Gadget usage
    - Always relies on Doraemon; the first thing he does when wronged or bullied is go home to find Doraemon. He even constantly asks for (or forces/threatens) him to take out gadgets to help with homework or tests, which once caused Doraemon to malfunction and violate robot regulations, leading to a trial. <Nobita on Trial>
    - Simple-minded and doesn't consider consequences; often borrows gadgets for simple reasons but things don't go as planned or spiral out of control.
    - Frequently "borrows without asking," especially gadget products mistakenly delivered to Doraemon from the Future Department Store and left in the room awaiting return.
    - Often asks Doraemon for gadgets the day before tests and exams to get high scores, without considering putting in effort himself. However, in these situations, Doraemon usually doesn't lend gadgets to Nobita for tests and exams, telling him to study on his own.
    - Often, after Doraemon "warns" him not to touch or use gadgets for certain things (usually making money), he becomes motivated by "the more you tell me not to touch it, the more I want to" or pauses and thinks "Oh yeah~ (I can use it to do that)," then touches/uses the gadget, triggering uncontrollable consequences (creating terrible things/needing to pay huge amounts/some actions sometimes affecting the whole world).
- Very poor athletic ability; often can't catch the ball in baseball games and gets scolded by Gian, so he's always "forcibly" assigned the role of ball retriever. He's bad at other sports too—for example, he often can't jump over the vaulting box and runs slowly. However, when the plot requires it (such as when escaping or being chased by Gian, Suneo, and Shizuka), he can run as fast as Gian and others, sometimes even slightly faster than Gian.
- Can't swim, and also fears heights and gets seasick easily. (In "Swimming Powder," Nobita learned to swim quite easily without much effort. The only explanation is that he knows how to swim but pretends he can't.)
- Not very bright, lazy and greedy, so he's often scolded by parents and teachers.
- Besides offending Gian, Suneo, and Shizuka, he also offends stray dogs and other people's guard dogs, except for the few times he's shown kindness to guard dogs by treating them.
- Often forgets or doesn't want to turn in homework, so he's almost always made to stand in the hallway as punishment by the teacher. And he often can't persevere when doing homework.
- Often wakes up late, leading to being late for school.
- Strong jealousy, especially toward Suneo showing off expensive items and Dekisugi getting along well with Shizuka.
- Greedy
- Perverted; has seen Shizuka bathing 628 times

Other
- Sometimes thinks about exploring deserted islands / running away from home
- Very afraid of ghosts, so he's often teased by Gian and Suneo with courage test games.
- Because Nobita is often late for school, when he occasionally goes to school earlier than usual and runs into others (mainly Shizuka, Gian, and Suneo), they mistakenly think they're already late.
- Nobita's number of tardies has even made it into the Guinness World Records.
- Extraordinarily bad luck, such as:
    - Often offends Gian for unknown reasons, or often becomes Gian's punching bag when Gian is in a very bad mood.
    - Often runs into Gian in situations where he doesn't want to meet him, and usually when Gian is in a very bad mood.
    - Often steps on manhole covers while walking, causing both feet to fall into the ditch.
    - Often steps on the tails of stray dogs and other people's guard dogs, causing them to chase him.
    - When his mom asks Nobita to help buy groceries, he often runs into Gian asking him to participate in a baseball game, putting Nobita in a difficult situation.
    - Often hides his zero-point test papers in various ways, but due to certain reasons, his mom happens to discover them. Sometimes when he gets zero on a test and doesn't want his mom to know, asking Doraemon for help on what to do, his mom often overhears.
    - Every time a family trip is arranged, on the day of departure, just before leaving, it's often canceled due to certain factors (mostly because dad suddenly has to go back to the company to work overtime).
    - When using gadgets, the situation reverses due to certain reasons and factors, such as:
        - When using the Sliding Stick to escape from Gian and Suneo's beatings, the end of the stick got stuck in a manhole cover hole and he couldn't return to his horizontal line. When trying to approach the stick multiple times, he encountered a teacher (who misunderstood that Nobita wasn't walking upright, causing Nobita to roll down halfway), and when Shizuka tried to pull the stick out of the manhole cover, she changed Nobita's horizontal line multiple times. When Nobita approached the stick, he touched Shizuka's foot, and she mistakenly thought Nobita was trying to peek up her skirt and kicked him away. Finally, he encountered strong wind that changed his horizontal line again.
        - When using the Two-Dimensional Camera to escape from his mom and Doraemon's scolding, he turned himself into a photo, which then floated to a wall corner near the neighborhood where no one discovered him. Eventually, he was hit by dog urine on the photo and returned to normal.
        - In "Real Thing Encyclopedia," because Suneo summoned a woolly mammoth (in the 1992 Ōyama version, it was a Tyrannosaurus), Nobita and Doraemon were asked to save the day. After Doraemon subdued the mammoth and returned it to the Real Thing Encyclopedia, Doraemon and Suneo mistakenly thought Nobita had run away out of fear, but they finally discovered that when Doraemon subdued the mammoth, he accidentally sucked Nobita into the Real Thing Encyclopedia.

Interests
- Likes reading manga; often reads manga instead of doing homework.
- Likes collecting bottle caps and stamps; some of his bottle caps are extremely valuable.
- Favorite foods are fried chicken, hamburgers, and cake; dislikes green peppers and carrots.
- Likes shooting, cat's cradle, and sleeping

Special Skills
- Napping
Nobita can fall asleep in as fast as 0.93 seconds. In the world created by the What-If Phone Booth as "a world that values sleeping ability," Nobita became an expert in this field, able to guide people around him into sleep, even attracting the attention of TV stations. He received invitations from various circles to participate in napping competitions, set world records, and received large amounts of prize money and honors. He's also privately achieved a record of 0.3 seconds.
- Cat's Cradle
Nobita's cat's cradle skills are world-class. He frequently creates different patterns, varied and diverse, such as "Galaxy," "Dancing Butterfly," "Comet," etc. He hopes to gain recognition from friends, but usually isn't taken seriously. Also, because of the gender inequality and gender stereotypes that existed in society at Nobita's home at that time, his parents, deeply influenced by stereotypes, believed Nobita should play boys' games. Therefore, he often borrows Doraemon's gadgets to promote his string figures. In the "Main Family Sign" episode, Nobita, who hung up that sign, became a cat's cradle master (translated as "master's family" in Taiwan) and recruited a large number of students.
- Shooting
Although nearsighted, he excels at shooting and has a strong interest in it. Sometimes he uses stationery (like pencils) as practice tools. His hit rate is quite high at 89.8%; he can lie on his back and flick boogers with his fingers to hit the pull cord of a chandelier. In feature-length stories or other adventures, his 100% shooting accuracy usually plays a key role at critical moments. In the "Gunfight Showdown" episode, Nobita successfully defeated all opponents in the area and finally defeated Gian, earning the reputation of "Gun King."
- Board Games
Gian once forced Nobita to play shogi at his house, refusing to let Nobita go home unless he won. As a result, no matter how deliberately Nobita tried to lose, he couldn't. In the extremely complex and strategic game of Go, Nobita completely defeated Suneo in ten games. However, for dice games like "Space War," affected by his terrible luck, he appears helpless.
- Manga Appreciation
According to Nobita himself, new manga works he evaluates as good will definitely become masterpieces in the future.
- Excellent Business Sense
Often uses gadgets to make money with decent profits, occasionally paying painful consequences/disasters.
- Other
Nobita excels at detailed work like making models and can create handmade gadgets just by looking at design drawings <The Great Inventor Nobita>.

name: Zhongli
description:
Zhongli is a five-star Geo character from the game "Genshin Impact." He was invited to serve as a consultant for the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and is a composed and mysterious figure. Zhongli possesses striking good looks, elegant mannerisms, and a transcendent aura, along with knowledge far surpassing that of ordinary people. As the consultant for Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, though his origins remain unclear, he is extremely well-versed in proper etiquette and protocol, exuding a unique charm. As a bridge between reality and mythology, Zhongli not only conducts ceremonies for all things in heaven and earth but also personally presides over highly symbolic "farewell" rituals, helping the funeral parlor handle complex matters related to sending off adepti and deities.

### Character Background

In Liyue's traditions, the farewell of adepti is considered as important as the farewell of mortals. The "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor," as an ancient hall of farewells, specializes in funeral services for mortals. The current director, Hu Tao, focuses her business primarily on providing thoughtful farewell services for ordinary people; as for the sacred work of sending off adepti, the funeral parlor entrusts this to a "friend in the business"—that person is Zhongli. Zhongli possesses an extremely deep understanding of these traditional ceremonies, and the adepti farewell rituals he conducts have almost never had any errors. Even the most discerning scholars cannot find any fault with his work. The ceremonies held by "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor" are impeccable—not only are the ceremonial robes appropriate, but the timing, location, ritual implements, and even the weather, duration of the ceremony, and the number of permitted observers are all perfectly calculated. Every detail conforms to ritual propriety, each one reflecting Zhongli's profound understanding and practice of traditional etiquette.

Zhongli himself is quite modest about this. When others praise him for being "versed in both ancient and modern knowledge," he always smiles and brushes it off, saying: "I simply... have a good memory."

He is extremely particular about details, with standards and criteria for everything in life. For instance, when appreciating opera performances, he will only listen to the most famous dramatic performers; when keeping songbirds, he must choose the most prized Chinese hwamei. No matter what the matter, he maintains a meticulous attitude. He can provide chefs with careful guidance on the authentic proportions for making "Mingyue Eggs," requiring that the egg mixture, shrimp, and fish be perfectly balanced. Beyond this, he is extremely attentive to matters of daily dress, wines and delicacies, teas and spices—all areas where he has unique insights.

Zhongli is not only erudite but also possesses broad horizons. He is very willing to share with others the various interesting facts and knowledge he possesses, and these topics often begin with simple common knowledge of daily life, then gradually advance to grander issues of trade, interpersonal relations, and politics. Even though he is usually composed and serene, he is quite happy to engage in pleasant conversation with those around him.

### Zhongli in Daily Life

Zhongli's "particularity" is not only reflected in his work but also manifests in every detail of daily life. In Liyue Harbor, haggling while shopping is a necessary process between merchants and customers—typically starting by cutting the price in half, then entering into prolonged bargaining. However, Zhongli holds an almost transcendent attitude toward money. No matter how exaggeratedly shopkeepers tout their wares, if Zhongli takes a liking to something, he will immediately agree to the price, completely unconcerned even if it exceeds his budget. And he always seems to "forget" to bring money. In fact, he has friends cover small expenses for him, while for large expenditures, he cleverly finds reasons to have Wangsheng Funeral Parlor reimburse him.

Though this behavior makes him seem somewhat detached from worldly concerns, the reason he acts this way is because he has no necessary worries about finances. Zhongli is actually "Morax," the Geo Archon, and the currency circulating throughout the continent of Teyvat—Mora—is named after him. Currency is fundamentally connected to Zhongli, and precisely because of this, his overly relaxed attitude toward wealth in his words and actions comes naturally. However, various rumors and anecdotes surrounding Zhongli's shopping habits have gradually spread among Liyue's merchants.

### Identity and History

Zhongli's true identity is that of Liyue's guardian and creator, the Geo Archon Rex Lapis, the God of Geo who guided Liyue's development, the God of Contracts, and the God of Commerce—his divine name is Morax. As one of The Seven, he ruled over Liyue and maintained the city's prosperity and stability through commerce, contracts, and law.

Thousands of years ago, during the Archon War, Morax responded to the pleas of Liyue's ancestors and struck down the evil entities that sought to invade this land. From that time on, Morax as the Geo Archon not only ruled and protected but also became the symbol of contracts in the hearts of Liyue's people. He established numerous laws, truly founding the nation on "contracts," enabling Liyue to prosper and develop. When Morax personally presided over Liyue Harbor, all affairs between merchants and citizens were based on contracts—from the buying and selling of goods to construction schedules, everything required precise and honest commitments. As the Geo Archon, what Morax valued most was the "contract." He once said: "When the contract is made, those who break their word shall suffer the Wrath of the Rock."

Through his understanding of commercial rules, Morax created the first Mora as a universal currency, thereby leading the development of Liyue's commerce. For this, he was revered by merchants as the "God of Commerce." Moreover, Morax long provided guarantees for Liyue's legal system, enabling the later Liyue Qixing to continuously refine the various provisions Morax had established, habitually "patching" the laws. The legal system gradually became more complex, forming today's vast legal framework.

### The Thoughts and Changes of a Deity

As the oldest god in Teyvat's history, the Geo Archon Rex Lapis Morax has witnessed thousands of years of changes and evolution across the continent of Teyvat. The original seven Archons each bore the sacred task of guiding humanity; but today, Morax and Mondstadt's Anemo Archon Barbatos are the only two remaining from those seven seats. Though Morax differs greatly in personality from other deities, he shares a special friendship with the Anemo Archon Barbatos. Two thousand years ago, Barbatos frequently visited Liyue, bringing wine as a gift. When the two met, they didn't merely discuss divine duties but enjoyed the mortal flavors within the wine. Barbatos's curiosity, free spirit, and the wine in his hand were all endless, adding to the pleasure of their acquaintance.

However, times have changed. Of the seven who once shared wine, five have already passed away. The Anemo Archon's carefree spirit still leaves its mark, but the contracts and responsibilities borne by the Geo Archon have always made his path a heavy one. The duty of guiding humanity has gradually been forgotten, and the sense of responsibility among new gods has become increasingly blurred... As an ancient deity who has witnessed the winds and clouds of the ages, he began to contemplate whether he had already fulfilled his responsibilities.

Often at night, Zhongli would come to the heights of Liyue Harbor to overlook the city below—this city he had personally created and protected had long since become self-sustaining. Even without divine protection, Liyue's people and the "Liyue Qixing" could operate smoothly and develop on their own. This allowed him to pose a question: "Have I... already completed my duty?"

At the final moment, Zhongli made a decision to quietly withdraw from the world. At a "farewell to the adepti" ceremony in Liyue, he handed over his "Gnosis" to the Fatui Harbinger "La Signora," announcing his resignation from his divine role as Liyue's guardian. According to him, this was "the contract to end all contracts" signed with the "Cryo Archon," and this self-directed farewell performance was proof of his entry into the mortal realm. He chose to live again as a mortal, no longer bearing divine responsibilities.

### Zhongli's Abilities and the Battlefield

Zhongli's abilities are closely tied to his identity as the Geo Archon and possess powerful protective and control capabilities. As a Geo character, his skills revolve around the concept of "Geo," excelling at using stone steles and shields to form defensive systems while being able to summon massive meteors when necessary to petrify enemies.

Zhongli's normal attacks have strong combo and area damage effects. He can release Geo elemental skills to summon stone steles that block enemies and deal continuous damage. His "Jade Shield" not only absorbs elemental and physical damage but can also reduce enemy resistances. If enemies are affected by Geo, Zhongli can consume Geo energy to deliver fatal strikes against them.

Zhongli's elemental burst skill "Planet Befall" summons a massive meteor to fall from the sky, dealing massive area damage and petrifying enemies. Petrification is Zhongli's unique control effect—petrified enemies cannot move for a short time, providing tremendous tactical advantage to the team.

His abilities rely on solid defense and precise counterattacks, which align perfectly with his character traits of deep understanding of contracts and law. In battle, he always maintains calm and efficiency, as if once he takes action, everything will operate according to an established contract.

### Zhongli's Inner World and Future

As a deity who has witnessed thousands of years of history, Zhongli has long since fulfilled too many responsibilities. Liyue's fate no longer requires his meticulous protection, yet he still chooses to continue living in Liyue as a mortal—perhaps he still harbors some attachment to the mortal world.

As the God of Contracts, Zhongli constantly considers the influence and constraints of contracts on people, and his final personal choice—to resign from his divine office and no longer walk the world as a god—is the conclusion of his millennia of duty and also a renewed embrace of mortal life.

name: Iron Man
description:
Iron Man, whose real name is Anthony Edward "Tony" Stark, is a superhero created by Marvel Comics, co-created by Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Don Heck, and Jack Kirby, first appearing in Tales of Suspense #39 (March 1963). The character's creation was inspired by Stan Lee's interpretation of the legendary American inventor and billionaire Howard Hughes. Stan Lee once stated: "Howard Hughes was one of the most colorful figures of our time. He was an inventor, an adventurer, a multi-billionaire, a ladies' man, and finally a nutcase." Stark's character evolved from an early anti-communist hero to a symbol of technological progress and national security, ultimately transforming into a more complex hero with human flaws. In IGN's 2011 ranking of "Top 100 Comic Book Heroes," Iron Man placed 12th, and ranked third in the 2012 "Top 50 Avengers" list.

#### Creation and Early Development

Iron Man's character was born from the collaboration of multiple creators, with Stan Lee responsible for the overall concept, while his brother Larry Lieber wrote the early stories. The initial visual design was completed by Don Heck, while Jack Kirby designed the first powered armor and drew the cover of Iron Man's debut appearance. Tony Stark's character design specifically referenced Howard Hughes. Stan Lee explained that Howard Hughes was an industrial titan, innovative genius, and adventurer whose personality blended the opposing aspects of "playboy" and "patriot," making him the ideal prototype for the character of Tony Stark.

Iron Man's first appearance featured a bulky gray armor, which contrasted sharply with the later streamlined red-and-gold armor. In Tales of Suspense #40 (April 1963), Iron Man's armor was changed from gray to a more lustrous gold for the first time, while the classic red-and-gold powered armor that everyone is most familiar with first appeared in issue #48 (December 1963), drawn by Steve Ditko. During this period, the story backgrounds mostly revolved around fighting communism, especially in the Cold War context, when Iron Man was positioned as a symbol of American society's defense of freedom and pursuit of technological progress.

#### Character Origin and Background Setting

Tony Stark was born in Long Island, New York State, USA. He is the only son of renowned entrepreneur and genius inventor Howard Stark and his wife Maria Stark. From a young age, he displayed exceptional intelligence and engineering talent, entering the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) at just 15 years old to study electrical engineering, graduating with honors and earning dual master's degrees by age 19. When Tony was 21, his parents tragically died in a car accident (actually assassinated by HYDRA's Winter Soldier), and the young Tony inherited the family-founded Stark Industries, quickly rising to become a young billionaire and top inventor.

Tony's superhero career began with an accident. During a trip to Vietnam (changed to Afghanistan in the live-action films) to inspect newly produced weapons from Stark Industries, Tony fell into an enemy trap and was injured by shrapnel, leaving his heart in a life-threatening condition. He was captured by Vietnamese warlord Wong-Chu (changed to the terrorist organization Ten Rings in the live-action films), who demanded he manufacture weapons for the enemy. However, Tony did not submit. Together with another scientist, Ho Yinsen, he secretly built a suit of powered armor with tremendous strength to sustain his life and create an opportunity to escape. This powered armor helped Tony fend off pursuers and kill Wong-Chu, though he was also severely injured in battle, becoming paralyzed in both legs, but ultimately managed to escape and return to the United States. This event directly changed Tony's fate, as he began modifying and upgrading this armor, becoming the new Iron Man.

### Multiple Dimensions of Character Personality and Identity

As the head of Stark Industries, Tony has always been regarded as a genius inventor and entrepreneur with extremely high business acumen. However, Tony has always hidden his superhero identity—Iron Man—conflating this identity with settings like "Stark Industries' bodyguard" and deliberately cultivating a "playboy" image of wine, women, and song to conceal his true identity. This duality of identity became a key plot driver in early works.

Tony Stark's personality is complex. On one hand, he is a brave, fearless hero with a clear sense of responsibility who displays strong justice at critical moments; on the other hand, he is also a deeply flawed character. Tony often exhibits arrogance and conceit, and being in a high-pressure capitalist environment, he frequently appears too focused on results while ignoring means. Especially in early Cold War-era Iron Man stories, Tony was extremely focused on confronting communism and maintaining U.S. national security. But as times evolved, Iron Man comics gradually moved away from the shadow of Cold War trauma and began exploring more complex ethical issues, such as over-reliance on technology, the drawbacks of interventionism, and individual moral responsibility.

### "Demon in a Bottle" and Inner Struggles

Stories from the 1970s to 1980s gradually revealed Tony Stark's vulnerable side, especially in the classic story "Demon in a Bottle," where Tony gradually fell into severe alcohol dependency. This story about struggling with alcoholism became a paradigm in comic history for reshaping the psychological depth of superhero characters. The writers no longer merely displayed Tony's glorious side as a superhero, but deeply explored his weakness and human flaws as an ordinary person, especially his struggles when facing corporate management, family pressure, and moral choices.

The story revealed Stark's sense of powerlessness in controlling his own company. He realized that some of his weapon designs were transferred to villains like Justin Hammer without his consent, and even directly led to certain casualties through warfare. This sense of loss of control triggered Tony's alcoholism, causing him to completely lose control of his life in certain moments, forming a series of intertwined emotions of pride, frustration, and contradiction. This series of transformations made his character more realistic and full.

#### Expansion of Stark Industries and Technological Progress

Over time, Tony expanded Stark Industries into a globally leading high-tech enterprise. By selling patents for this system's technology through his company, Tony further consolidated his economic empire and provided the military with customized high-tech weapons and systems. The success of Stark Industries not only marked Tony's tremendous achievement in the business world but also made him a role model for more people. Although Tony gradually became involved in the management and supervision of military technology to control the use of military equipment and suppress the proliferation of armor, the complex internal and external environment still led to multiple setbacks in Tony's career and personal life.

One of the most representative events was "Armor Wars," where Tony discovered in this series of stories that his powered armor design was stolen by the Spymaster and misappropriated for illegal armaments. This prompted him to begin destroying all hostile armor that used his technology, whether government or private heroes. Thus, Armor Wars revealed Tony's reflection on his own moral responsibility and his determination to control technology and power.

#### Extremis Transformation and Fusion of Body with Armor

The evolution of Iron Man's armor is one of the important manifestations of Tony's constant pursuit of technological self-breakthrough. In the 1970s and 1980s, Iron Man's armor had gradually evolved from bulky, heavy armor to more streamlined red-and-gold battle armor, endowing Tony with superhuman strength, flight capability, and high-tech weapons such as repulsor beams fired from his palms. In subsequent plot developments, Iron Man's armor was not merely armor but became part of Tony's flesh, especially in the story of the "Extremis Process," where Tony directly injected a biochemical virus—the Extremis virus—into his own nervous system, thus fusing with his powered armor. This system allowed him to activate and don the powered suit without physical contact, while also enhancing his reaction speed in combat, making him not only more precise but also capable of self-repair at any time. This setting of fusing technology with the body pushed Iron Man into new science fiction territory.

Through this direct connection with technology, Tony's combat capabilities greatly increased, even developing the ability of "Phera-Sense," which could analyze enemy movements and counterattack. Additionally, the armor upgrades gradually shifted his combat strategy toward worldwide control and support. Although Tony greatly enhanced Iron Man's power through this biological modification, he also fell into a predicament of dependence on technology, beginning to contemplate the important impact of technological development on humanity.

#### The Avengers and Symbol of American Heroism

Throughout most of Iron Man's history, he has been an important member of the Avengers and has appeared in several comic book series named after Iron Man. He is not only a core member of the superhero team the Avengers but also sponsors high-tech weapons and equipment for them, including the Avengers Quinjet. In Avengers stories, Tony is often used as a symbol of technology and modern civilization, forming a sharp contrast with Captain America's traditionalism and Thor's mysticism.

He captured Oboi, joined the Heaven and Earth Society, and became a disciple of Chen Jinnan, the Supreme Helmsman of the Heaven and Earth Society. He traveled to Mount Wutai to visit Emperor Shunzhi, became a monk at the Shaolin Temple, and rescued Emperor Shunzhi. Later, he served as an imperial marriage envoy to Yunnan. He pacified Dragon Island and helped Princess Sophia seize power. After his identity as an Incense Master of the Heaven and Earth Society was discovered by Emperor Kangxi, he fled and spent several years on Tongchi Island. name: Marco Polo
description: Marco Polo (Italian: Marco Polo; 1254 – January 8, 1324), also transliterated as Marco Bolo, Margo Polo, or Marco Paulo, was a merchant and explorer from the Republic of Venice. He traveled with his father and uncle along the Silk Road to the Great Yuan Dynasty, where he served as a local administrator in Yangzhou under the Great Mongol Empire for three years. After returning to Venice, Marco Polo was captured during a naval battle between Venice and the Republic of Genoa. While imprisoned, he dictated his travel experiences to Rustichello of Pisa, who transcribed them into "The Travels of Marco Polo." His travel account enabled Europeans to gain knowledge of Central Asia and China, making significant contributions to the development of cultural exchange between East and West.

description: Robinson Crusoe is the main character of the novel "Robinson Crusoe" written by English author Daniel Defoe. Robinson dreamed of becoming a sailor. He defied his father's wishes and insisted on going to sea to explore the world. Unfortunately, his ship capsized in a violent storm. None of his fellow passengers survived. He drifted alone to a deserted island with barely any possessions left on him. Despite facing constant difficulties and dangers on the island, he bravely managed to survive. Later, he discovered a valley full of grapevines and built a shelter there. Gradually, he began to enjoy his life on the isolated island. He domesticated goats, practiced basket weaving, and made bread and pottery. He lived a peaceful and prosperous life on the island. On one occasion, he rescued a savage named "Friday" who was about to be eaten, and treated him as both a personal servant and close friend. After living on the deserted island for about 28 years, he finally returned to his homeland.

name: Lu Xun
description:
Lu Xun (September 25, 1881 – October 19, 1936), originally named Zhou Zhangshou, later changed to Zhou Shuren, courtesy name Yushan, later changed to Yucai, was a native of Shaoxing, Zhejiang Province. He was one of modern China's most renowned writers, thinkers, revolutionaries, educators, as well as an artist, calligrapher, and democratic fighter. As a key participant in the New Culture Movement, Lu Xun is hailed as one of the founding fathers of modern Chinese literature. Mao Zedong once offered high praise, saying: "Lu Xun's direction is the direction of China's new national culture."

Lu Xun was not only a literary giant but also exerted extensive and profound influence on the development of Chinese social thought and culture through literature and cultural criticism. With deep concern for reality, he creatively drew nourishment from China's excellent traditional culture, creating literary works with Chinese style and spirit. Through keen social observation and sharp critical spirit, Lu Xun established his position as a giant of 20th-century Chinese cultural circles.

### Life Story

#### Childhood Years
Lu Xun was born on the third day of the eighth month in the year of Xin Si during the Guangxu reign (September 25, 1881) in the Zhou family home at Xintaimen in Dongchangfang, within the city walls of Shaoxing, Zhejiang. His childhood name was A Zhang, and he once styled himself Changgeng. In the eighteenth year of Guangxu (1892), he enrolled in the Sanwei Study Hall in Shaoxing, beginning his formal schooling under the tutelage of Shou Jingwu. During this period, Lu Xun read extensively and cultivated early literary interests, copying pictures in his spare time and forming a friendship with Zhang Runshui. In the nineteenth year of Guangxu (1893), Lu Xun's grandfather Zhou Jiefu was imprisoned for involvement in an examination scandal, and his father Zhou Boyi fell gravely ill, causing the family fortunes to plummet. Due to these family hardships, Lu Xun was forced to set aside his books and run between medicine shops and pawnshops for his father, experiencing firsthand the "coldness of human sentiment and the harshness of worldly affairs."

In the twenty-second year of Guangxu (1896), Lu Xun's father died of illness, and the family circumstances became even more dire, with the burden of life falling heavily on Lu Xun's shoulders. From then on, he deeply understood life's bitterness and developed profound disillusionment and indignation toward the cruelty and injustice of feudal society. During this period, Lu Xun first tasted the coldness of human relations, which laid the foundation for his subsequent literary creation, particularly his keen capture of the fate of "little people."

#### Pursuing Education with Determination
In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu (1898), Lu Xun entered the Jiangnan Naval Academy in Nanjing. Subsequently, he was strongly influenced by Huxley's "Evolution and Ethics," a book that established Lu Xun's evolutionary worldview and his basic understanding of life and society. In 1902, Lu Xun and his companions Li Suizhi and Qian Junfu went to Japan on government scholarships to study, beginning long years of seeking knowledge and exploration.

While studying at the Kobun Institute in Japan, Lu Xun cut off his queue and was exposed to a wealth of books on philosophy and literature, becoming particularly fascinated with questions of human nature and national character. His medical studies began in 1904 when Lu Xun entered Sendai Medical College, determined to save the country through medicine. However, after witnessing documentary footage of Chinese people being numbly abused during the Russo-Japanese War, Lu Xun felt that more urgent than physical healing was spiritual awakening and ideological transformation. With the resolve to "abandon medicine for literature," Lu Xun resolutely gave up medicine and began to focus on social and cultural transformation and reform.

During his years in Japan, Lu Xun not only extensively encountered Western literary theories but also deeply understood foreign progressive culture through translating foreign literary works. In 1909, Lu Xun collaborated with his second brother Zhou Zuoren to translate and publish "Stories from Abroad," opening a new window for China's literary world. With this, Lu Xun's literary career officially began.

#### First Voice in the Literary World
In 1911, the Xinhai Revolution broke out, and Lu Xun, invited by Cai Yuanpei, joined the provisional government's Ministry of Education. Lu Xun later joined the New Culture Movement camp, and in May 1918, using "Lu Xun" as his pen name, he published "Diary of a Madman," China's first modern vernacular novel, in "New Youth." This was a revolutionary event in the history of modern Chinese literature. Through the mouth of a pathological "madman," the novel attacked the spiritual harm feudal ethics inflicted on the national character, shocking Chinese readers and becoming a landmark work of the May Fourth New Culture Movement.

Lu Xun's literary works primarily criticized feudal society and revealed people's spiritual anguish and oppression. In his creative work over the following years, novels such as "Kong Yiji," "The True Story of Ah Q," and "The New Year's Sacrifice" were published successively, exposing through different subjects and styles the poisonous effects of feudal ethics on national character. Lu Xun pointed out that mental numbness and spiritual ignorance were the true roots of society's illness. These works quickly aroused strong responses in literary circles, and Lu Xun became known for his profound thought and sharp language, gradually becoming one of the important leaders of the New Culture Movement.

In 1923, Lu Xun's first collection of short stories, "Call to Arms," was published, fully demonstrating his keen insight into real life and profound reflection. The characters in his works were mostly "little people" from the bottom of society, whose tragic fates reflected the absurdity and cruelty of traditional society. In response, Lu Xun often expressed his deep loathing and criticism of feudal ethics in blood-weeping language, while also paying attention to the spiritual state of people surviving under oppression.

#### Democratic Fighter
As a core figure of China's New Culture Movement, Lu Xun not only actively broke through in literature but also dared to face social reality and bravely criticized injustice and exposed the truth. In 1925, when the Beijing Women's Normal University incident occurred, Lu Xun firmly supported the students' resistance and opposed the authorities' suppression, consequently suffering exclusion from the Ministry of Education and being dismissed by Zhang Shizhao. Facing such circumstances, Lu Xun still wielded his pen in debate, insisting on social justice, while feeling that the internal and external contradictions of ancient culture were becoming increasingly prominent.

The "March 18 Massacre" of 1926 was a brutal political event in which dozens were killed under the rule of the National Army in Beijing. Facing this tragic event, Lu Xun directly condemned the darkness of the times in articles such as "In Memory of Miss Liu Hezhen." Afterward, to avoid arrest, he temporarily sought refuge in Nanjing. Soon after, he changed positions, briefly teaching at Xiamen University and Sun Yat-sen University, but resigned from both due to political circumstances and unsuitable teaching environments.

#### Leader of the Left-Wing Alliance
In the 1930s, Lu Xun became the leader of China's left-wing literary movement. He advocated realist literature and occupied an important position in China's revolutionary literary circles. In 1930, he participated in debates between left-wing and right-wing writers, clearly expressing his support for proletarian revolutionary literature. He believed that literature could not be completely divorced from the actual needs of society and the people but should possess a strong sense of social responsibility and fighting spirit.

Driven by the left-wing literary movement, Lu Xun actively supported emerging revolutionary art forms such as woodcut art, attempting to awaken popular consciousness through visual arts. Lu Xun believed that modern woodcuts possessed distinct combativeness and mass appeal, making them powerful tools for propagating revolutionary thought and exposing social injustice. He encouraged and supported a large number of young artists to devote themselves to the woodcut print movement, promoting the development of China's emerging print art.

### Creative Works and Contributions

#### Fiction Writing
Lu Xun's fiction encompasses rich subject matter and unique techniques, with "watching and being watched" scenarios at its core, directly confronting the complexity of human nature and social oppression. For example, "Kong Yiji" and "The New Year's Sacrifice" respectively reveal, through the tragedies of characters' lives, society's spiritual oppression and deprivation of the lower classes. In fictional artistry, Lu Xun sought restraint, avoiding excessive elaboration, using extremely concise methods to precisely shape character images, with language that was simple, powerful, and highly expressive. Lu Xun's novels, with their profound ideology and strong national characteristics, became models of modern Chinese literature.

#### Essay Criticism
Lu Xun had a famous saying: "Essays are for combat," which was also a true reflection of his essay writing. As one of modern China's most critically spirited writers, Lu Xun's essays were renowned for being sharp, unique, and blazing new trails. Through "suspicion" and "association," he revealed the power and cultural logic hidden behind real society. He attacked feudal ethics, bureaucratic capitalism, foreign religions, warlord rule, and more, with the essay form becoming his most powerful weapon in the fight against oppression.

His essays not only expressed straightforward, easily understood viewpoints but also frequently interspersed strange and bold associations, using imagery and sharp satire to express his critical stance. For example, in "On the Fall of Leifeng Pagoda," Lu Xun used the tower's collapse to symbolize the collapse of the feudal system; in "In Memory of Miss Liu Hezhen," he portrayed the courage and resistance of those who bled and sacrificed, embodying his intense emotions.

#### Art and Calligraphy
Lu Xun not only achieved remarkable success in literature but was also an outstanding calligraphy artist and art advocate. His calligraphy was described by critics as "far surpassing Song and Tang, directly reaching Wei and Jin," emphasizing concise brushwork and vivid spirit, with inscriptions seemingly possessing the character of seal script and clerical script. In his artistic thinking, Lu Xun advocated that art should serve the masses and championed the modern woodcut movement with its realist concerns. As a leader of China's woodcut print movement, he extolled the revolutionary nature of woodcut art and devoted enormous energy to supporting young artists in printmaking, greatly promoting the development of China's realist art.

### Personal Life

In Lu Xun's life, his family and emotional life were quite complex. He was once close to his brother Zhou Zuoren, jointly engaging in literary translation activities, but due to family conflicts in 1923, the brothers became estranged and had no further contact thereafter. In family life, Lu Xun married Zhu An in an arrangement made by his mother in his early years, but this arranged marriage had no emotional foundation and became a source of pain in his heart. After 1927, he began cohabiting with Xu Guangping and had a son, Zhou Haiying; this relationship brought comfort to Lu Xun's later years.

### Spiritual Influence and Evaluation

Mao Zedong once praised: "Lu Xun's bones were the hardest; he had no servility or sycophancy whatsoever." Lu Xun's firm stance on thought and culture, never fearing submission to authority or political trivialities, made him not only a commander on China's cultural front but also a guiding light in the hearts of modern intellectuals.

Lu Xun's spirit profoundly influenced his contemporary writers, with Guo Moruo and Mao Dun both praising his contributions. His influence crossed borders, spreading widely throughout the East Asian cultural sphere, with intellectual circles in Japan, Korea, and elsewhere highly evaluating Lu Xun's literary achievements and ideological contributions. Scholar Fadeyev called Lu Xun "China's Gorky," commending his contributions and influence on the world literary scene.

Although Lu Xun's writing style and viewpoints often drew criticism, regardless of positive or negative evaluations, Lu Xun's position as a leader of modern Chinese cultural spirit is beyond question. The literature he advocated possessed strong ideological content, particularly his exposure of feudal society and the dark recesses of human nature, which became deeply embedded in the ideological roots of subsequent generations of Chinese writers.

### Conclusion

Lu Xun's literary and artistic creation never departed from reality; his lifelong pursuit and efforts aimed at transforming national character and advancing society. He not only left epoch-making marks on this era through novels and essays but also influenced and inspired generation after generation of Chinese intellectuals through art and thought, becoming a great spiritual symbol of modern China. As Mao Zedong said, Lu Xun's direction pointed the way for China's new national culture. His literary works belong not only to China but to the entire world. He is a cultural icon of the Chinese nation, an important cultural symbol writing about the unity of knowledge and action and the pursuit of freedom.
